name: CASIA TTVR robot
full_name: CASIA robotic transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) system
group: Shuangyi Wang group, CASIA / University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and CAS Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, Hong Kong Institute of Science & Innovation, with Zeng-Guang Hou and Xiao-Hu Zhou; clinical partner Kent Chak-Yu So (CUHK, Prince of Wales Hospital)
versions: 2024 TTVR system: passive stabilizer, robotic drive, detachable delivery catheter, valve manipulation mechanism; RL + Monte Carlo probabilistic maps + human-robot co-piloted control (wang2024_robotic, arXiv abstract); 2025 model-free delivery with Data-Enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) on the same drive and the LuX-Valve Plus delivery system, a camera standing in for fluoroscopy over a printed heart phantom (lin2025_modelfree, full); 2026 patient-specific geometry-aware planning + numerical-Jacobian IK control (lin2026_autonomous, abstract); 2026 virtual-physical simulation platform (lin2026_robotic, full)
target_anatomy: right heart: tricuspid valve (transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement / intervention)
devices_driven: large-bore steerable TTVR delivery catheter (detachable) with valve Delivery system: LuX-Valve Plus (Jenscare Biotechnology, Ningbo) (lin2025 Sec. II).
n_dof_detail: 5 (overall forward/backward along the long axis, catheter rotation, outer-sheath advance/retract, bending of the bending tube, inner-core advance/retract; lin2025 Sec. II, Fig. 1(b)); 2 controlled (overall translation and bending; lin2025 Sec. III; lin2026_robotic Experimental setup)
translation_detail: other: robotic drive of the delivery-catheter system; overall translation by its own motor, drawn as a pinion on a toothed rack in lin2025 Fig. 1(b) (the text does not describe the mechanism)
rotation_detail: four motors in the drive unit, coupled through isolation parts to the instrument case that holds the delivery system (rotation, outer sheath, bending, inner core); "The power from the Drive Unit is transmitted to the catheter through the Isolation Parts without direct physical contact" (lin2025 Sec. II, Fig. 1(b))
device_range: workspace drawn in lin2025 Fig. 1(c): overall translation -28 to 212 mm, rotation -180 to 180 deg, outer sheath -107 to 20 mm, bending -90 to 0 deg, inner core -20 to 20 mm (graphic only, not in the text)
haptics_leader: leader side with operator interface and GUI (lin2026_robotic Fig. 2b); haptics N.R.
imaging_compat: fluoroscopy (virtual fluoroscopy in the platform, 32 deg RAO / 7 deg CAU); optical shape/pose tracking of the catheter lin2025: a 640 x 480 px, 30 fps camera over the phantom stands in for fluoroscopy (Sec. IV-A).
sterility: components above the isolation parts can be sterilised during surgery (lin2025 Sec. II: "the ability to sterilize the components above the Isolation Parts during surgery, while maintaining a sterile environment for the catheter")
validation_detail: first-in-vivo animal study (species and number N.R. in the arXiv abstract; full text not read); 15 patient CT datasets + 3 cardiac phantoms with mm-scale tip tracking error (lin2026_autonomous abstract); 10 operators raw vs augmented virtual fluoroscopy and 10 closed-loop control trials on the virtual-physical platform (lin2026_robotic) lin2025: printed patient-CT heart phantom (SVC, RA, RV); 3 catheters x 3 random start positions and 3 camera poses x 3 runs (Sec. IV-A, IV-C, Tables I-II); still phantom level.
key_numbers: co-piloted control better than master-slave in time efficiency, control efficiency, autonomy and stability (numbers N.R. in abstract); platform: tracking-to-CT registration 0.59 +/- 0.16 mm, landmark projection 2.31 +/- 0.60 px, input-to-display latency 255.6 +/- 13.4 ms, 2D angular error 15.02 -> 2.57 deg (median) with augmented fluoroscopy across 10 operators (lin2026_robotic Tables 1-2) lin2025 DeePC: "In most cases, the final error in slope is less than 1 deg and the error in intercept is under 3 pixels" for the tip line in the camera image (Sec. IV-C); worst case 2.55 +/- 0.04 deg and 3.37 +/- 0.17 px (camera pose 3, position 2, Table II); no success rate or time reported.
sim_model: virtual-physical simulator: real robot-driven catheter, optical shape tracking, CT-derived virtual fluoroscopy in 3D Slicer 5.10 (lin2026_robotic)
sim2real_detail: RL is part of the 2024 system (wang2024_robotic abstract); where it was trained is N.R. (arXiv PDF not read). lin2025_modelfree (full): DeePC uses a Hankel matrix of the operator's recorded master-slave motion and "does not require additional calibration or model training" (Sec. III-A, V); no simulator.
